working_time_convention.note: Analytical full-time convention: 40 hours per week × 52 weeks / 12 months.

minijob.note: Monthly earnings threshold for marginal employment in 2026.

employer_flat_rates.source: Minijob-Zentrale 2026 flat-rate schedule for commercial (gewerblich) minijobs, aggregated via 2026 payroll guidance (getminijob.de, minijobgenie.de)
employer_flat_rates.note: Employer-only flat-rate contributions on gross pay for a commercial minijob. Employee side is modelled at 0%: minijob workers are subject by default to compulsory pension insurance with a 3.6% top-up unless they file for exemption (Befreiung von der Rentenversicherungspflicht); the large majority exercise this exemption in practice, so the reference scenario models the opt-out case as an explicit, adjustable assumption.

midijob.note: German transitional employment range, also known as Übergangsbereich.

gleitzone_2026.source: Cross-checked 2026 payroll guidance (lohndialog.de, betanet.de); coefficients agree to 9 decimal places, indicating both quote the same GKV-Spitzenverband/Minijob-Zentrale published Faktor F.
gleitzone_2026.note: beitragspflichtige_Einnahme_total = total_base_coefficient x gross + total_base_constant (base for the combined employer+employee contribution, at each branch's total rate); beitragspflichtige_Einnahme_employee = employee_base_coefficient x gross + employee_base_constant (base for the employee's own-rate contribution, at each branch's employee rate). The employer's contribution is the residual: total contribution minus the employee's contribution, which concentrates the Übergangsbereich relief on the employee side.

standard_job.note: Regular employment regime above the upper Midijob threshold.

methodological_limits: Income tax is excluded from V1.
Net wage is computed before personal income tax.

Mini-jobs are modelled with the 2026 employer flat-rate schedule and 0% employee contribution (opt-out from the pension top-up assumed); midi-jobs are modelled with the 2026 Übergangsbereich Gleitzone formula (Faktor F).
Private health insurance is excluded from V1.
Individual sickness-fund additional contribution rates are not modelled in V1.
The health additional contribution is modelled with a reference average rate.
Accident insurance contributions are excluded from V1.
